name: Harrison Ford
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1968), Ford had only minor uncredited bit parts in films like Dead Heat on a Merry-Go-Round (1966) and A Time for Killing (1967); his breakthrough came with American Graffiti (1973) at age 31 and Star Wars (1977) at 35.
early_history_summary: Ford graduated from Ripon College in 1960, discovered acting in his senior year, and signed with Columbia Pictures' new talent program in 1964 at $150/week. He made his film debut as an uncredited bellhop in 1966 but struggled with minor roles and turned to carpentry to supplement his income.
family_context_summary: Son of an advertising executive (formerly an actor) and a stay-at-home mother; grew up in the Chicago suburb of Des Plaines.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was briefly an actor before becoming an advertising executive; no sustained industry mentorship or direct film access documented.
evidence_summary: Ford was a self-described late bloomer who discovered acting by accident in college. By 26, he had only minor uncredited film roles and was supplementing his income as a carpenter. His father's brief acting career did not provide meaningful industry access. Fame arrived at 31 with American Graffiti and 35 with Star Wars.

name: Alfonso de Portago
milestone_by_age_26: Named the world's leading amateur steeplechase rider in 1951-52 (ages 23-24) and rode the Grand National twice as a gentleman rider before making his Ferrari racing debut at age 26 in 1954.
early_history_summary: Born to Spanish aristocracy as 11th Marquess of Portago, Portago grew up between Madrid and Biarritz with access to horses, planes, and high society. He became a champion amateur steeplechase rider by his early twenties, rode the Grand National twice, and transitioned to motorsport in 1953-54 when he joined Scuderia Ferrari through Ferrari importer Luigi Chinetti.
family_context_summary: Born to Spanish aristocracy as heir to the Marquess of Portago title; his godfather was King Alfonso XIII. He was a millionaire with no financial concerns, raised between Madrid and Biarritz.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was president of Puerta de Hierro and a prolific golfer who died after a polo match; his grandfather was Minister of Public Instruction and Mayor of Madrid. No direct equestrian or motorsport domain transfer documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: aristocratic wealth, multi-sport access, fearless temperament, Ferrari connection
evidence_summary: Portago's early success was built on aristocratic wealth and status that gave him access to expensive sports — steeplechase riding, bobsleigh, and motorsport — without financial constraints. He was the world's leading amateur steeplechase rider by age 23-24 and transitioned to Ferrari racing at 25-26. His fearless temperament and physical talent across multiple sports were noted by contemporaries, though he lacked the technical grounding of peers who built careers through grassroots competition.

name: Tom Selleck
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1971), Selleck had only bit parts, commercials, and a Fox talent program contract; his breakout role as Magnum P.I. came in 1980 at age 35.
early_history_summary: Selleck transferred to USC on a basketball scholarship, where a drama coach suggested acting. He joined the 20th Century Fox New Talent program in 1967 and appeared on The Dating Game, but had only minor commercial and bit-part work through his early twenties.
family_context_summary: Father was a real estate investor and executive who moved the family from Detroit to California; mother was a homemaker. Family was supportive of risk-taking.
evidence_summary: Selleck had no acting experience before college and entered the Fox talent program at 22 with zero prior training. By 26, he had only commercials and bit parts. His breakout came at 35 with Magnum P.I. in 1980, after 11 years of minor roles and unsold pilots.

name: Clint Eastwood
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1956), Eastwood had only uncredited bit parts in Universal films like Revenge of the Creature (1955) and Tarantula (1955); his break came with the TV series Rawhide in 1958 at age 28.
early_history_summary: Eastwood was drafted during the Korean War and stationed in California. After discharge in 1953, he moved to Hollywood and secured a Universal contract in April 1954 at $100/week. He was criticized for his stiff manner and spent 1954-1956 in uncredited minor roles before being dropped by Universal.
family_context_summary: Family moved frequently during the Great Depression before settling in Piedmont, California in 1940. Father worked various jobs; not documented as having entertainment industry connections.
evidence_summary: Eastwood entered acting late after military service, securing a Universal contract at 24 through a chance encounter. By 26, he had only uncredited bit parts and was criticized for his acting ability. His career breakthrough came at 28 with Rawhide (1958), and international fame at 34 with the Dollars Trilogy.

name: Ágota Kristóf
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1961), Kristóf was working in a clock factory in Switzerland after fleeing Hungary in 1956; her first novel was not published until 1986 at age 51.
early_history_summary: Kristóf was born in Csikvánd, Hungary to a teacher and an arts professor. At 21, she fled the Soviet suppression of the Hungarian Revolution with her husband and infant daughter, settling in Neuchâtel, Switzerland. She worked in a clock factory for years while learning French, the language in which she would eventually write.
family_context_summary: Parents were Kálmán Kristóf, an elementary school teacher, and Antónia Turchányi, a professor of arts. Her husband was her former history teacher at school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were educators but not in the literary domain; no direct writing or publishing industry access documented.
evidence_summary: Kristóf's literary career was delayed by decades of displacement and factory work. After fleeing Hungary at 21, she spent years as a factory worker in Switzerland, learning French from scratch. Her first novel was published at 51, making her a late-blooming writer whose early adversity shaped but did not accelerate her literary output.

name: Vin Diesel
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1993), Diesel had only childhood theater roles and bouncer work; his first self-made film Multi-Facial was completed in 1995 at age 28, and his breakthrough came with Saving Private Ryan in 1998 at 31.
early_history_summary: Diesel began acting at age 7 at the Theater for the New City in Greenwich Village after breaking into the theater with friends. He continued in Off-Off-Broadway productions through his teens and twenties while working as a bouncer for nine years. He attended Hunter College for creative writing but dropped out to pursue acting.
family_context_summary: Raised by his mother Delora, an astrologer, and adoptive stepfather Irving Vincent, an acting instructor and theater manager. He has a twin brother, Paul. Biological father was not present.
parent_family_domain_summary: Stepfather was an acting instructor and theater manager, providing early exposure to theater and performance; this directly led to Diesel's childhood stage debut at age 7.
evidence_summary: Diesel had early theater exposure through his stepfather's connections and acted from age 7, but by 26 had no film credits or material career milestone. He spent years as a bouncer while auditioning. His career launched at 28 with the self-funded short film Multi-Facial (1995), which screened at Cannes and attracted Spielberg's attention.

name: Audrey Hepburn
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Academy Award for Best Actress for Roman Holiday (1953) at age 24 and a Tony Award for Best Leading Actress in Ondine (1954) at age 25, becoming the first actress to win an Oscar, Golden Globe, and BAFTA for the same performance.
early_history_summary: Hepburn studied ballet at the Arnhem Conservatory during WWII and performed to raise money for the Dutch resistance. After the war she trained under Sonia Gaskell in Amsterdam and Marie Rambert in London, then worked as a chorus girl in West End productions. French novelist Colette spotted her in 1951 and insisted she play Gigi on Broadway, launching her to stardom.
family_context_summary: Born to a Dutch baroness and an Anglo-Irish father who was a fascist sympathizer; parents divorced when she was six. The family lost its fortune during WWII, and her mother worked as a cook and housekeeper to survive.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct performing arts domain transfer from parents; her mother's aristocratic connections facilitated access to ballet training and cultural institutions but not film industry access.
primary_early_advantage_tags: ballet training, wartime adversity, aristocratic connections, West End pipeline, Colette discovery
evidence_summary: Hepburn's early career was shaped by wartime adversity — starvation, resistance work, and family displacement — combined with years of ballet training at the Arnhem Conservatory and later under Marie Rambert in London. Her aristocratic mother's connections facilitated access to cultural institutions despite the family's lost fortune. The pivotal moment came when French novelist Colette spotted her filming in Monte Carlo and insisted she play Gigi on Broadway (1951), which led directly to her casting in Roman Holiday (1953) and her Academy Award at age 24.

name: Didier Deschamps
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1993 UEFA Champions League with Marseille as the youngest captain ever to lift the trophy, and won two Ligue 1 titles (1990, 1992), all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Deschamps started football at age 8 at Aviron Bayonnais in Bayonne, was spotted by Nantes scouts, and joined their elite academy at 14. He made his Ligue 1 debut at 16 on September 27, 1985, and accumulated over 100 league appearances for Nantes before transferring to Marseille in 1989, where he won two league titles and the Champions League.
family_context_summary: Born in Bayonne in the French Basque Country to Pierre and Ginette Deschamps; not much documented about family financial status or parental professions beyond working-class origins.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite academy, early pro debut, mentor coach, French football system, Basque Country football culture
evidence_summary: Deschamps' early trajectory was driven by France's elite football academy pipeline: he joined Nantes' renowned youth system at 14, debuted professionally at 16, and accumulated over 100 Ligue 1 appearances by his early twenties. Mentor Jean-Claude Suaudeau at Nantes promoted him to the first team. The move to Marseille in 1989 placed him in a top European club where he won two league titles and the Champions League as the youngest ever captain at age 24. His early departure from home at 14 and loneliness at the academy created urgency and resilience.

name: Gerd Binnig
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1973), Binnig had only completed his bachelor's degree in physics; the scanning tunneling microscope was invented in 1981 at age 34, and the Nobel Prize came in 1986 at 39.
early_history_summary: Binnig decided to become a physicist at age 10 but spent much of his university years playing in a beat-band. He gained a bachelor's degree from Goethe University Frankfurt in 1973 and remained to do a PhD in Werner Martienssen's group, completing it in 1978 before joining IBM Zurich.
family_context_summary: Son of a milliner and an engineer; grew up in post-war Frankfurt playing in the ruins of demolished buildings. Family was not wealthy but supported his education.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an engineer, which may have influenced his early interest in physics, but no direct scientific domain transfer or mentorship documented.
evidence_summary: Binnig showed early interest in physics from age 10 but spent his university years more focused on music than research. By 26, he had only a bachelor's degree with no notable research output. His career-defining work — the scanning tunneling microscope — came at 34, with the Nobel Prize at 39. His father's engineering background may have sparked his interest but did not provide direct research access.

name: Ivana Trump
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1975), Trump was working as a ski instructor and model in Canada; her business career began after marrying Donald Trump in 1977 at age 28, with executive roles at the Trump Organization in the 1980s.
early_history_summary: Born Ivana Zelnickova in communist Czechoslovakia, she began skiing at age 4 and joined the junior national ski team. She married Austrian ski instructor Alfred Winklmayr in 1971 to obtain an Austrian passport, then emigrated to Canada where she worked as a ski instructor and model promoting the 1976 Winter Olympics.
family_context_summary: Father was an electrical engineer and mother was a telephone operator in communist Czechoslovakia; middle-class family living on the grounds of the Bata shoe-factory complex in Gottwaldov.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father encouraged her skiing abilities from age 4; no business or real estate domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Trump's early life was defined by competitive skiing and a marriage of convenience to escape communist Czechoslovakia. By 26, she was a ski instructor and model in Canada with no business achievements. Her business career was entirely a product of marrying Donald Trump in 1977 and receiving executive roles in the Trump Organization during the 1980s.

name: Alberto Korda
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1954), Korda was working as a beginner wedding and banquet photographer with poor technical quality; he founded Korda Studios in 1956 at 28, and his iconic Che Guevara photo was taken in 1960 at 32.
early_history_summary: Born Alberto Diaz Gutierrez in Havana to a railway worker, Korda took many jobs before becoming a photographer's assistant. He shot banquets, baptisms, and weddings, running back to his studio to develop film. The quality of his early work was very poor, with images becoming blurry and paper yellowing after a few months.
family_context_summary: Son of a railway worker in Havana, Cuba; working-class background with no documented financial privilege or artistic family connections.
evidence_summary: Korda came from a working-class Havana family and taught himself photography through trial and error. By 26, he was a beginner photographer with poor technical skills doing weddings and banquets. His career took off after founding Korda Studios in 1956 and becoming Cuba's first fashion photographer, leading to his role as Castro's unofficial state photographer and the iconic 1960 Che Guevara portrait.

name: Romy Schneider
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved breakthrough stardom at age 17 with the title role in Sissi (1955), which became one of the most successful German-language films of the era and spawned a trilogy that made her a major international star by her early twenties.
early_history_summary: Born into a three-generation theatrical dynasty — father Wolf Albach-Retty was a leading Vienna actor, mother Magda Schneider was a major German film star, and grandmother Rosa Albach-Retty was a celebrated theater actress — Romy made her film debut at 15 alongside her mother in When the White Lilacs Bloom Again (1953). Her stepfather managed her career, and she achieved massive stardom with the Sissi trilogy starting at 17.
family_context_summary: Born into a prominent theatrical family: father Wolf Albach-Retty was a leading actor at Vienna's Volkstheater, mother Magda Schneider was a major German film star, and paternal grandmother Rosa Albach-Retty was one of Austria's most popular theater actresses. Parents divorced when she was five; her stepfather Hans-Herbert Blatzheim later managed her career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents and paternal grandmother were professional actors, providing direct industry access, on-set exposure, and name recognition that led to Romy's film debut alongside her mother at age 15.
primary_early_advantage_tags: acting family, mother's film access, early screen debut, career managed by stepfather, three-generation theatrical dynasty
evidence_summary: Romy Schneider's early career was a textbook case of family-domain apprenticeship: both parents were famous actors and her grandmother was a theater legend, giving her direct film industry access from birth. Her mother Magda Schneider arranged her film debut at 15 in When the White Lilacs Bloom Again (1953), and her stepfather managed her career. The Sissi trilogy (1955-57) made her one of the most popular actresses in German-language cinema by age 19. While she had natural screen presence, her early opportunities were overwhelmingly a product of inherited family access rather than independent achievement.
